words.asked:
**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** John: "the UI issues trace back to one of my very first rules: no build step… it's the biggest target of the Theseus method… We don't need to tidy it all, but it's a perfect example where we can leave it better than we found it." The first slice (LIN-4446) served a pure server file to the browser at `/shared/` and retired the browser's copy. Its blind read found the cost: a bridge turns the shared file back into a global, with a load-timing rule that four files explain and nothing checks, and a second shared file would need a second bridge. On the direction, John: "I feel there's a sensible engineering approach, that a skilled developer would take… Excellent, that sounds like a great solution." Today the browser area has 44 script files that share through globals, `public/common.js` is 3,309 lines and `public/observation.js` 5,019, over 100 unit test files load browser scripts as classic scripts, and the area's note holds 10 Waiting entries.

**What we want.**

* Pages become ES modules that import what they share, as browsers do natively. Still no build step and no framework.
* Shared logic is imported, not restated: each converted view drops its copies.
* A bridge back to a global is only a temporary ramp for pages not yet converted: one at most, and visibly shrinking.
* The tests get simpler as views convert, not more elaborate.
* Taken one view at a time, each piece finishing one move and naming what it retired. John on size: "Happy for it to be whatever size is natural."
* No view is retired unless John rules it. The side rail and the visual refresh (LIN-4342, LIN-4343) come after, on the cleaner code.

**Done when**

* the slice 1 bridge is gone, or the only one left and shrinking under a check;
* the area's Waiting entries are settled, or say why not;
* the area reads better in a blind read after this work than before it, by more than an untouched area read at the same times.

**Every change names what it retires. Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself; only John's calls (product, money, authority, what to retire) go to him as rulings.

fields.says:
**Piece 2 — one real page, top down** (as built, PR #2436)

* `public/task-page.js` is an ES module: the IIFE and the `typeof module` / `module.exports` seam are gone, and the page exports its pure rules and render helpers by name. The renderer's last `SCRIPTS` entry in `lib/render-task-page.js` is `{ module: '/task-page.js' }`. Its one DOMContentLoaded listener still registers last; it writes no `window.*`, so nothing is added to the bridge. Golden diff: the seven script tags only, to `type="module"`.
* Duplicates: the plan's name-equality search finds only a coincidence (`init`). The real copies were `formatElapsed` (= `fmtDuration`) and `relativeWords` (= `relativeAgo`). They now have one home, the served leaf `lib/time-words.js` (`SHARED_MODULES` entry, owner front-end-pages); the page imports it, and server callers import it directly instead of via `render-run-steps.js` / `task-page-loader.js` re-exports. This is a serving change the plan did not have (decision-98, resting on question-84's if-unanswered course). The classic copies in `session.js`, `observation.js`, `live-console.js` stay, listed in the area's Waiting entry.
* Tests: piece 1 already built `import-world.js`. Pure exports are plain static imports with no world; the DOMContentLoaded suites share a new 36-line `tests/unit/helpers/task-page-world.js`. Migrated: `task-page-client`, `task-timeline-client`, `task-page-question` (`makePage`), `lin-3975-proposal-refresh` (URL helper), `lin-3975-task-run-links` (its vm run). Re-anchored on names, not migrated: `lin-3975-summary-and-time`, `lin-3975-task-run-control`, `lin-3975-chat-fold`; the `relativeWords` probe became a test of the exported `shareTime(doc, value, now)`.
* Census: 102 → 100 (only `task-page-client` and `task-timeline-client` leave; the others still load another classic file).
* Docs: the module-capable-loader Waiting entry is deleted (piece 1 had shown its premise wrong); `source-map.md` calls `task-page.js` a module and gains a `time-words.js` entry.
* Behaviour change: `fmtDuration(Infinity)` is `null` where the page printed `Infinityh`; no page path passes a non-finite span. Pinned by `lin-4472-time-words.test.js`.
* Shortfall against "each migrated suite reads shorter": most are shorter by a few lines; `lin-3975-task-run-links` grew by 4 (its replacement clock test), and `lin-3975-task-run-control` and `lin-3975-chat-fold` were only re-anchored, so are unchanged in length.

Witnesses run: each migrated suite green after conversion; mutation of `fmtDuration` failed `lin-4472-time-words` and `lin-3975-task-run-links`, then passed restored; `grep module.exports|typeof module public/task-page.js` empty; `tests/e2e/task-page.spec.js` + `task-timeline.spec.js` 18 passed locally; 175 targeted suites green (5,539 + 122 tests); full unit suite left to CI.

index.says: A page script's second request keeps the poll's discipline: coalesce every reason into one fetch per window, and stop when the poll stops (hidden tab, 401, revoked link). `createTimelineRefresher` (`public/task-page.js`, LIN-4405) is the pattern; a running chip changes the poll's track about once a minute, so "fetch when it changes" alone repeats. Done reads once more first (`finish`): the poll that says done carries the last change, and stopping drops it.

Shared leaves: a shared module is a leaf (it imports nothing and names no browser or Node global, `tests/unit/shared-modules.test.js`), served only through the explicit `SHARED_MODULES` allow-list in `lib/vendor-assets.js`, one route per file under the served /lib/ namespace, never by directory (a lib file not on the list is a 404). A page imports one with a relative specifier that starts with ../lib/ (quoted in the code). That resolves to the same file in the browser and in Node only because `public/` is served at the URL root and stays flat, with no nested .js files (`tests/unit/front-end-import-layout.test.js`). Do not move `public/` under a prefix or add a subdirectory.

A `{ module }` entry's place in a renderer's script list means nothing: a module runs after every classic script, wherever it is listed. A bridge reader is safe because of when it reads the global, not where the shim sits.

A converted page is tested by plain `import` over the fake DOM (`tests/unit/helpers/import-world.js`), not by `loadWorld`. Each import is a fresh module instance, and the world puts every global back when it is restored. The classic-loader census (`tests/unit/classic-loader-census.test.js`) is a ratchet on the suites that still load classic scripts: it may only fall. A suite that runs a classic file through `runClassic` counts, except `public/chart-helpers.js` and `public/close-out.js`, the two IIFE siblings a module page may read.

A test that cuts a browser script's source by an indented marker (`'  function init(doc) {'`, `'    function toggle(row) {'`) breaks on any re-indent, such as removing an IIFE to make a module: `indexOf` gives -1. Test an export instead, or anchor on a name with no leading whitespace. `lin-3975-task-run-control` and `lin-3975-summary-and-time` are the examples (LIN-4472).
PR #2436 (LIN-4472, piece 2 of LIN-4463): task page as an ES module, suites as imports, lib/time-words.js served leaf

`importWorld` (`tests/unit/helpers/import-world.js`) installs only the globals it is given, nothing more. Test a converted page's pure exports by a plain static import, with no world at all; drive a page's init (its DOMContentLoaded listener) through `tests/unit/helpers/task-page-world.js`, which builds the world the task page needs, rather than restating that setup in each suite (LIN-4472).

F1. `tests/unit/lin-3975-task-run-links.test.js` must read shorter (plan-10: each migrated suite reads shorter; it grew 228 to 232). Move the test `the page's running clock paints fmtDuration's words for every span it can show` (currently `:211-221`) into `tests/unit/lin-4472-time-words.test.js`, inside its `describe`, and change that file's import to `import { shareTime, tickClocks } from '../../public/task-page.js';`.
